reason: Kunjed Gyalpo ch.32 has the yogin abide in 'the non-conceptual intention of the dharmakāya' when resting unaltered in how things appear

Mipham's buddha-nature as the union of luminosity and emptiness corresponds to the awareness Dzogchen introduces; partial because the sūtra term names the potential, the Dzogchen term the recognized presence
Both name the root ignorance of saṃsāra; Dzogchen specifies it as non-recognition of the ground's display (Tsigdön Dzöd topic 2)
Longchenpa's all-base is the basis of karmic traces, like the Yogācāra ālaya, but kept distinct from the all-base consciousness
Bön's kun gzhi is the ultimate ground; the Nyingma kun gzhi is not — the equivalence holds only across the two traditions' vocabularies and is contested
The bardo of becoming corresponds to the intermediate existence between death and birth; the six-bardo scheme extends the word to life, dream, meditation, dying and dharmatā
The ground luminosity introduced at death is described as one's own awareness, empty and luminous — the luminous mind of the sūtras
Bön's three-body scheme parallels the Buddhist trikāya; Bön insists on its own lineage for the scheme
